title: Levy-distance invariance estimate
statement:
There are constants $K,A>0$ such that the following holds. Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability spaces, and let $F$ be a multilinear coefficient family of degree at most $k$ whose Boolean-cube evaluation has variance at most $1$. For $\varepsilon\ge0$, suppose every coordinate influence of that evaluation is at most $\varepsilon$. If $X$ and $Y$ are independent coordinate families on the respective spaces, each coordinate is $(2,3,\rho)$-hypercontractive for some $0<\rho<1$, and each has mean zero and second moment one, then the Levy distance between the laws of $F(X)$ and $F(Y)$ is at most
\[
K\left(\frac1\rho\right)^{Ak}\varepsilon^{1/8}.
\]
